Because insight is absent, the history almost always comes from a family member. Cholinesterase inhibitors are not indicated and can worsen behavioural symptoms, so management centres on specialist diagnosis, non-pharmacological behavioural strategies, caregiver support, and early attention to driving, financial capacity and advance planning.
key_points: Preserved memory and navigation with prominent behavioural change is the pattern that separates it from Alzheimer disease
Loss of insight means collateral history is essential
Cholinesterase inhibitors are ineffective and may worsen behaviour
Early diagnosis enables decisions about driving, work and financial capacity while some capacity remains
explanation.pearls: Address driving and financial capacity at the first consultation rather than at review: disinhibition and impaired judgement with absent insight make these patients dangerous on the road and vulnerable to financial exploitation well before their memory scores fall.

options.rationale: Cholinesterase inhibitors are not effective in this disorder and frequently worsen behavioural symptoms and agitation, because the cholinergic deficit that underlies their benefit in Alzheimer disease is not the pathology here. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

Antipsychotics are used sparingly and briefly for severe behavioural disturbance, and long term use in any dementia carries increased stroke and mortality risk, so it is not the primary management strategy. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

Early onset dementia with prominent behavioural change, loss of insight, dietary change and executive impairment while memory and navigation are preserved, alongside asymmetric frontotemporal atrophy, indicates behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia. Management is specialist assessment with behavioural and caregiver support, and cholinesterase inhibitors are specifically avoided because they can worsen behaviour. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

Apathy is easily mistaken for depression and this diagnosis is frequently made first, but he has no subjective low mood, no guilt and no sleep or appetite loss in the usual pattern, and the imaging shows structural disease. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

A two year progressive course with objective executive impairment and unequivocal atrophy on imaging is established disease, and delay costs the family the practical, financial and legal planning that early diagnosis permits. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Psychotropic)

explanation.summary: The acute syndrome of erythema nodosum, bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, arthritis and fever is a recognised presentation of sarcoidosis with an excellent prognosis, remitting spontaneously in the great majority of patients. It is one of the few settings in which the diagnosis is accepted on clinical and radiological grounds without tissue confirmation. The treatment decision is therefore not which immunosuppressant to use but whether to treat at all, and the answer for uncomplicated disease is symptomatic management with observation. Corticosteroids are reserved for organ threatening involvement, meaning progressive pulmonary impairment, hypercalcaemia, cardiac, neurological or sight threatening ocular disease.
key_points: Symmetrical bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy with clear lung fields distinguishes this from tuberculosis and lymphoma
Biopsy is not required when the clinical picture is characteristic
Baseline assessment includes calcium, renal function, electrocardiogram, spirometry with gas transfer and ophthalmology review
Serum angiotensin converting enzyme is neither sensitive nor specific and should not drive treatment decisions
explanation.pearls: The electrocardiogram and the eye review are the two easily forgotten parts of the baseline workup: cardiac sarcoidosis can present with nothing more than conduction delay, and asymptomatic uveitis found on slit lamp examination converts an observe only plan into one requiring treatment.

options.rationale: Corticosteroid is indicated for progressive pulmonary disease, hypercalcaemia, cardiac, neurological or sight threatening ocular involvement, none of which is present, and it exposes a woman with a self-limiting illness to months of avoidable adverse effects. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Respiratory)

Tuberculosis causes hilar lymphadenopathy but characteristically asymmetric or unilateral, and her interferon gamma release assay is negative with no exposure history and no risk factors. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic)

Tissue confirmation is required for atypical presentations, but this triad is considered sufficiently characteristic that biopsy is not needed, and the procedure carries risk without changing management. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Respiratory)

The combination of erythema nodosum, bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, ankle arthritis and fever is an acute presentation of sarcoidosis that remits spontaneously in the large majority of patients within one to two years, so symptomatic treatment with an anti inflammatory drug and structured observation is appropriate. Systemic corticosteroid is reserved for organ threatening disease, which she does not have. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Respiratory)

Second line immunosuppression is for chronic disease requiring prolonged corticosteroid or for steroid failure, and starting it in an illness that usually resolves by itself is disproportionate. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Respiratory)

explanation.summary: Amiodarone contains a large iodine load and causes thyroid dysfunction in a significant minority of patients, and distinguishing the two forms of thyrotoxicosis it produces determines the treatment. The iodine induced form arises in a gland with underlying nodularity or latent autoimmune disease, involves excess synthesis, shows preserved or increased vascularity on colour flow Doppler, and responds to thionamides. The destructive form occurs in a structurally normal gland, releases preformed hormone from damaged follicles, shows absent vascularity, and responds to corticosteroid. Mixed forms occur and are treated with both. Whether to continue amiodarone is a joint decision with cardiology, since its long half life means cessation gives no rapid benefit.
key_points: Colour flow Doppler vascularity is the practical discriminator between the two forms
Radioiodine is ineffective because the iodine load suppresses uptake
Amiodarone has a half life of weeks, so stopping it does not achieve short term control
Amiodarone more commonly causes hypothyroidism, which is treated with thyroxine while the drug continues
explanation.pearls: Do not assume stopping amiodarone is the answer: in a patient whose arrhythmia was refractory to everything else, withdrawal may precipitate the very rhythm disturbance that a thyrotoxic heart tolerates worst, and the decision belongs jointly with cardiology.

options.rationale: Thionamides block new hormone synthesis and are effective in the iodine induced form, which shows increased vascularity in a nodular or enlarged gland. They have little effect when preformed hormone is being released from a destroyed gland. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Endocrinology)

Iodine uptake is profoundly suppressed by the large iodine load from amiodarone, so radioiodine cannot be delivered to the gland and the treatment is ineffective in this setting. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Endocrinology)

Cessation may be appropriate but amiodarone has a half life of many weeks so withdrawal alone does not control thyrotoxicosis in the short term, and stopping it can destabilise the arrhythmia it was prescribed for. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Endocrinology)

Surgery is reserved for severe disease failing medical therapy or requiring rapid control in a patient who cannot stop amiodarone, and adding further iodine to an already iodine loaded patient is counterproductive. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Endocrinology)

Absent vascularity on colour flow Doppler with negative receptor antibodies and no goitre indicates a destructive thyroiditis releasing preformed hormone rather than increased synthesis, and this form responds to corticosteroid rather than to thionamides. Joint endocrine and cardiology input is needed because the decision about continuing amiodarone depends on the arrhythmia risk. (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Endocrinology)
